findings.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernameForm.java:47 — P1 (confidence 100%): `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` calls no API supplied by `UsernameForm` or its superclass (the only added method is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel)`), breaking the subclass/base type contract and preventing the service module from compiling.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernameForm.java:47 — [P1, confidence 100, anchor 100] The changed re-authentication gate `if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())` invokes a zero-argument method although the only added helper is `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`, so this change cannot compile and none of the added re-authentication acceptance coverage can run.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java:160 — [P1, confidence 100, anchor 100] The new gate `return webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null;` suppresses `fillContextForm` for every anonymous initial login, so the changed code no longer serializes the conditional-passkey UI/challenge needed by the newly added initial-login tests before any user is selected.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java:65 — [P2, confidence 75, anchor 75, advisory] When conditional passkeys run during re-authentication, `return false;` suppresses `ALLOWED_AUTHENTICATORS`/identified-user inclusion while the sibling `SHOULD_DISPLAY_AUTHENTICATORS` gate remains user-derived and true, producing contradictory rendering flags that can expose an empty authenticator display; the strongest rebuttal is that the template ignores the display gate without an authenticator list, but that fails because this change explicitly claims to suppress authenticator display yet does not propagate that sibling gate or verify the rendered state.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernameForm.java:47 — P1 confidence 100 anchor 100: the verbatim `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` invokes no matching method because the inherited helper requires `UserModel`, so javac rejects the services module before any re-authentication flow can run.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java:53 — P2 (confidence: 91%; verbatim: `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context);`): a re-authentication passkey error/cancellation reaches `createErrorResponse` without any changed test exercising that callback or asserting the hidden-username/registration-disabled form state, so a regression in this newly added error recovery path ships undetected; the password-error test is not a substitute because it invokes `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler`, not this WebAuthn error callback.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java:65 — P2 (confidence: 84%; verbatim: `return false;`): the changed tests cover passkeys-enabled users and a realm with passkeys disabled but never re-authenticate a selected user in a passkeys-enabled realm who has no passwordless credential, so an unconditional conditional-UI form or a password-flow break in this new branch ships undetected; the disabled-policy test cannot rebut this because it bypasses `isPasskeysEnabled()` entirely.

goldens.comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims there's a contradiction between ALLOWED_AUTHENTICATORS and SHOULD_DISPLAY_AUTHENTICATORS flags, but examining the diff shows that shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() returning false simply prevents the WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean from being created and added to the form context. The method fillContextForm() checks shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() and only adds authenticator data when true. When false, no authenticator list is added at all - there's no contradictory state. The finding misreads the code flow: returning false from shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() means the authenticator list section is simply not populated, not that conflicting flags are set.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the new call to AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context) in WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse() (line 53) is not directly tested by any new test case. Looking at the diff, the new tests (webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication, webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication, etc.) test successful passkey re-authentication flows but don't specifically test the error/cancellation path in createErrorResponse. The test webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey tests password errors during re-authentication, but as the finding notes, that goes through badPasswordHandler, not the WebAuthn error callback. This is a legitimate concern about missing test coverage for newly added error handling logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java:65 — P2 (confidence: 84%; verbatim: `return false;`): the changed tests cover passkeys-enabled users and a realm with passkeys disabled but never re-authenticate a selected user in a passkeys-enabled realm who has no passwordless credential, so an unconditional conditional-UI form or a password-flow break in this new branch ships undetected; the disabled-policy test cannot rebut this because it bypasses `isPasskeysEnabled()` entirely.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a potential gap in test coverage. Looking at the diff, the new method `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` in WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator returns `false` unconditionally (line 65). The tests added cover: (1) passkeys-enabled users doing re-authentication, (2) users without passkeys in a realm with passkeys disabled. However, there's no test for the specific scenario of a user who is already selected (re-authentication context) in a passkeys-enabled realm but who lacks passwordless credentials. This is a valid observation about incomplete test coverage for the new conditional logic, though the actual behavior may still be correct - the finding is about missing test coverage rather than a confirmed bug.
